title: Guided Setup Wizard + Placeholder Experiences for New Projects
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: New teams creating projects in the Redwood Console often land on sparse dashboards with little guidance, causing confusion about next steps (model selection, routing, cost controls). Purpose: Design a compact guided-setup wizard plus template-aware placeholder states and micro-education surfaces (tooltips and inline guides) to reduce time-to-first-success and reduce support tickets. Goals: 1) reduce new-project time to first successful API call to under 10 minutes, 2) reduce ‘where do I start’ support tickets by 40% in first 30 days, 3) increase template adoption for starter workloads to 30% of new projects. Scope: three flows — (A) first-time project wizard (one-page progressive form), (B) contextual placeholder cards for empty dashboards and routes, (C) in-product micro-education (tooltips, short checklist, template gallery).
comments: 2025-11-12: Kickoff with PM & Eng. Agreed success metrics and scope. PM suggested adding a cost-estimate step for the wizard.
2025-11-14: Low-fidelity wireframes reviewed with Growth (Liam Chen) — feedback: emphasize clear CTA for ‘Run sample call’ and keep advanced options collapsed.
2025-11-16: Mid-fi Figma uploaded; initial prototype covers three wizard steps + placeholder cards. Linked for dev handoff (see design_links).

2025-11-18: Usability testing (5 participants). Key takeaway: users prefer example outputs and an immediate ‘Try it now’ button; tooltip text should avoid jargon (replace ‘KV cache’ with ‘response cache’).
2025-11-19: Design review with Eng leads (Rohit Patel) — blocked by API for sample-run telemetry; Eng asked for a minimal stub endpoint. Action: ENG-3210 to provide stub API by 2025-11-24.
2025-11-20: Incorporated copy edits from PM (Sofia Alvarez) and accessibility pass. Submitted for final review.
2025-11-20: Requested design QA slot with Frontend on 2025-11-25.
decisions: Use a single-screen progressive wizard instead of a multi-step modal to reduce context switching.
Place a persistent micro-education bar at top of project pages showing progress (0/4 steps) — dismissible and resumable.
Provide three starter templates (Chatbot, Q&A, Embeddings index) with pre-filled settings; templates load sample data and a ‘Run sample call’ button.
Keep advanced configuration in an ‘Advanced’ collapse to avoid overwhelming first-time users.
Empty-state artwork will be simple vector illustrations following brand tokens; avoid heavy animations for performance.
Tooltips will be optional and opt-in per user; default to on for first 14 days after account creation.
user_research_notes: Tested with 5 engineers (mix of ML infra and product teams). Average completion time for first sample call in prototype: 7m 40s.
Quote: 'Seeing a sample response immediately made me comfortable to tweak prompts' — participant ID P3.
Pain: unclear cost visibility during template selection; added inline cost-estimate line items to the wizard.
Participants confused by 'model variants' phrasing — replaced with 'model size' and concrete latency estimates.
accessibility_considerations: All interactive elements follow 4.5:1 contrast ratio; tooltip content accessible via keyboard focus.
Wizard uses semantic HTML landmarks and ARIA live regions for status updates on long-running sample calls.
Images have alt text; illustrations have text-only fallback for screen-reader-first experience.
next_steps: ENG-3210: deliver sample-run stub API and telemetry by 2025-11-24.
Design QA with Frontend on 2025-11-25 (assign engineers and checklist).
A/B test two micro-education strategies: top progress bar vs inline checklists (run for 4 weeks).
Finalize copy variants and ship i18n keys for English + EU locales.
Prepare handoff package for Dedicated/private UI tweaks (in case customers disable sample-run endpoint).
